text:
maya: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel switch to block-sr14 we saw p99 jump in us-east. GPU util went ~70% -> 92% and tail latency spiked. I'm thinking about a short-lived "catch-up window" idea to avoid immediate shedding: temporarily allow slightly bigger microbatches and enable aggressive KV-prefetch to drain backlog for a bounded time. thoughts? :thinking:

jun: can you paste the numbers you saw?

maya: perf snapshot from 2026-03-17 02:14 UTC:
```
region: us-east-1
workload: chat-service-prod
baseline (before): p50=24ms p95=82ms p99=160ms gpu_util=71%
after switch: p50=26ms p95=110ms p99=442ms gpu_util=92%
queue_depth: avg 9 -> 48
kv_cache_hit: 0.81 -> 0.62
```

jun: hmm. flamegraph points to longer kernel tail for sequences >256 and microbatching causing more KV misses because batches reorder requests (prefetch window misaligned). might be the kernel selector choosing the attention kernel that's high-throughput but worse tail for mixed seq lengths.

rachel: main SLO is p99 <= 200ms for this customer tier. Temporary "bigger microbatches" sounds risky — could make p95 worse for short queries. we need priority for short requests and a safety cutoff.

tom: propose hybrid approach:
- short-request prioritization (seq_len <= 64) always routed to low-latency fast-path threads
- catch-up windows triggered only when queue_depth > 40 for > 200ms and GPU util > 85%
- during a catch-up window: increase microbatch cap by +30% (bounded) and enable aggressive KV-prefetch for impacted models
- enforce max catch-up window duration of 150ms and cool-down of 5s
This drains backlog but keeps windows short so new arrivals still see low p50/p95.

maya: sketch of config I had in mind (draft):
```yaml
admission:
  short_path_seq_len: 64
  catchup_trigger:
    queue_depth_threshold: 40
    sustained_ms: 200
  catchup_action:
    microbatch_increase_pct: 30
    max_duration_ms: 150
    kv_prefetch: aggressive
    priority_mask: "short-first"
  cooldown_ms: 5000
```

jun: found a repro for the kernel selector regression: selector uses floor(seq/64) to pick quantized path but due to integer rounding it skipped int8 for seqs exactly divisible by 64. quick fix is to use ceil or explicit boundary. this explains why some mixed batches ended up on the slower kernel. repro steps below:
```
# repro
echo seq=128 > /tmp/seq.txt
./kernel-picker --seq $(cat /tmp/seq.txt) --model xlm-8b
# expected: int8_fast_path, got: block_sr14_slow_path
```

rachel: good catch. if we patch selector + add catch-up windows we still need canary testing. loadtest targets: p50/p95/p99 + kv_hit + gpu_util and also histogram of tail kernel durations.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary for kernel-fix + catchup-config scheduled to 3 pods in us-east-1 at 2026-03-17T03:00Z. TTL: 10m. tagging: canary=capture-runaway.

maya: thanks. i'll run a short soak with synthetic mixed-seq load (short-heavy + occasional long) and attach results. initial expectation: p99 should drop <200ms if kernel selector fixed and catch-up windows bound correctly.

tom: add runtime trace tag `catchup=on` and `kernel_pick=updated` so we can slice metrics by requests that experienced catch-up windows. also make sure admission still rejects long-running low-priority jobs when queue still > threshold after two windows.

jun: one more note — KV hit recovery might lag because prefetch warms asynchronously. consider prefetch primes (warm first 2 tokens) when entering catch-up windows, not just on full batching. that helps long sequences start with warmed KV.

rachel: scheduled loadtest run: 03:10Z -> 03:22Z, I'll post dashboards. if canary looks good, roll to 25% traffic and monitor p99 jump regressions for 30m. :thumbsup:

maya: perfect. i'll post the soak logs and a short diff for the kernel selector patch here once available. thanks all. :rocket:
